sentences.text: Anatosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms named for its broad, duck-like snout.
The broad, flattened shape of the Anatosuchus skull developed as the animal matured.

The premaxillae are broad and flat, each holding six recurved teeth that point backward, while the maxillae contain nineteen small recurved teeth and the lower jaw bears twenty-one teeth on each side.
The largest teeth in the skull are located at the corners, and the teeth were small and subconical with little wear, suggesting they were not heavily used for grinding.
The proatlas vertebra is an inverted V-shaped bone with a dorsal keel that is quite large relative to the atlas.
The neural spines on the cervical vertebrae grow taller along the series, with the third being twice as tall as long and the seventh almost five times as tall as long.
The osteoderms on Anatosuchus are trapezoidal in shape and quite pitted.
The manus features very large fourth digits with six phalanges instead of the usual four.

The humeri are long, straight, and quite slender with a width of less than 10% of their length, the ulnae are relatively curved, and the radiales are strong, heavy bones that are almost as wide as the radii.
It is currently unknown what evolutionary benefit the specialized six-phalanged fourth digits provided.
Anatosuchus was described by a team of paleontologists led by American Paul Sereno in 2003, and the genus was named by Sereno et al. in 2003 with the only known species being Anatosuchus minor.
The type species A. minor was named to reflect the animal's small body size, and the animal was described based on a juvenile specimen consisting of an almost complete skull with articulated jaws.

Fossils of Anatosuchus were found in the Elrhaz and Echkar Formations in Gadoufaoua, Niger, dating to the Late Aptian or Early Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous, specifically between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
A 11 mm toothless section of the lower jaw likely formed a cutting edge used with the front upper teeth to process prey.
Despite its duck-like appearance, Anatosuchus is considered to have eaten small aquatic creatures.
Anatosuchus is an extinct genus of notosuchian crocodile classified within the family Uruguaysuchidae.
Initial descriptions suggested Anatosuchus formed a monophyletic clade with Comahuesuchus within Notosuchia, though this is disputed.
